text:
maria: Quick question — we're prototyping geo-priority routing + model-variant fallback for hosted API. Goal: pick lowest-latency region for a customer tier, but if latency > threshold or capacity constrained, fall back to a compatible model variant in another region or a cheaper quantized variant. Any strong objections to the approach?

aj: Sounds good. Two quick concerns: (1) how do we compute "latency" (client RTT vs server p99)? (2) how do we avoid oscillation if we keep switching regions? :thinking_face: 

maria: Good call. Thinking we use observed request p95/p99 from last 60s for region candidates, plus a static network-probe baseline. If observed p95 > config.threshold then don't route there. For oscillation we add sticky windows + decay and require sustained violations for 30s before switch.

nate: +1. Also need to track per-customer SLOs. A PLG free-tier customer might prefer cheaper model even with slightly higher latency. Enterprise customers want lowest latency even if cost is higher. We need tier-aware scoring.

sophia: We should encode scoring as a simple cost function: score = alpha*latency_ms + beta*cost_per_token + gamma*fallback_penalty. Admins can set alpha/beta by tier. Example policy could be: 
```yaml
policy_id: geo_priority_01
match: customer.tier in ["enterprise","pro"]
regions: [us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1]
latency_threshold_ms: 120
weights:
  latency: 0.7
  cost: 0.2
  fallback_penalty: 0.1
sticky_seconds: 45
fallback_variants:
  - name: llama-70b-q4_1
    cost_multiplier: 0.6
    compatible: true
  - name: mosaic-32b-int8
    cost_multiplier: 0.4
    compatible: true
```

j: (typo) @sophia i meant to tag you — this is what we need for console UX too.

kevin: How do we represent "capacity constrained"? Do we have a single capacity gauge per region per model? We already expose running_instances and queued_requests. Maybe a simple capacity_score = 1 - min(1, queued_requests / provisioned_capacity). If capacity_score < 0.2 mark as constrained.

maria: That works. We should also incorporate tail latency and recent error rate. If error rate > 1% in last 5m, mark region unhealthy.

infra-bot: deploy:policy-evaluator v0.12.0 started applying new scoring function to staging.

aj: Telemetry needs: region, model_variant, chosen_score, latency_ms, fallback_reason, customer_tier, route_version. Without those we can't debug. Also please emit a boolean 'sticky_switch' when we override sticky window.

sophia: Agreed. Telemetry event schema suggestion: 
```json
{
  "timestamp": "...",
  "customer_id": "...",
  "customer_tier": "enterprise",
  "request_id": "...",
  "candidate_regions": ["us-west-2","us-east-1"],
  "selected_region": "us-west-2",
  "selected_variant": "llama-70b-q4_1",
  "latency_ms": 98,
  "p95_region_ms": 120,
  "capacity_score": 0.85,
  "fallback_reason": "latency_threshold_exceeded"
}
```

maria: For the console, product wants a simple toggle + quick preview: "Prefer low latency" / "Prefer low cost" and an advanced JSON editor for policy power users. We should surface estimated cost delta and estimated p95 impact in the preview.

nate: UI-wise we should show a per-route timeline of region selection decisions for last 30 minutes with hoverable reasons. That will save ops calls.

kevin: Edge case: what if model variant compatibility differs by region (some regions only have quantized build)? Policy should include allowed_variants per region, policy evaluator must only consider those.

sophia: Add to DSL: allowed_variants_by_region: { "us-west-2": ["llama-70b-q4_1"], "eu-west-1": ["mosaic-32b-int8","llama-70b-q4_1"] }

aj: Another operational concern: when the primary region is degraded we might want to stream partial responses from fallback model while continuing to attempt primary (graceful degradation). Do we want streaming fallback? That is more work.

maria: We should support a "degraded-mode" fallback where the platform returns a lower-fidelity variant but marks response with header `x-redwood-fallback: region|variant|reason`. Customers can opt-in per route.

infra-bot: alert:policy-evaluator p95_latency > 3000ms in eu-west-1 for model llama-70b-q4_1 (detected 5m ago).

kevin: Seeing that alert now — we should prevent routing to eu-west-1 for enterprise routes until devs triage. Can we flip a soft-lock in the evaluator?

maria: Yes, we need an administrative soft_lock API that sets region_state: { eu-west-1: "suspended" } and it should be visible in console with expiration and reason.

aj: Implementation plan: 
- API: /routing/policies (GET/PUT) 
- Evaluator: add metrics-based region filter + sticky window + capacity_score check 
- Telemetry: add chosen metrics and fallback_reason enum 
- Console: quick toggles + preview + timeline 
- Ops: soft_lock endpoint + incident integration

sophia: I'll draft the policy schema PR. @maria can you own the telemetry spec? @kevin can you take the evaluator changes? I'll pick up console wireframes after schema PR.

maria: Yep I'll carve out telemetry spec this sprint and include example dashboards (p95 by route, fallback_rate, cost_delta).

kevin: Will start on evaluator changes, will push a staging branch and ping infra-bot for canary.

nate: Also suggest we add a metric "fallback_penalty_applied" in logs so we can quantify how often cheaper variants are chosen because of penalty parameters.

aj: One more UX ask: expose a simulation endpoint so customers can POST a sample request and get back predicted region/variant and estimated latency + cost. That helps onboarding.

maria: Love that. We'll prototype simulation in the console preview.

infra-bot: note: policy-evaluator v0.12.0 applied to staging at 1764988820.

sophia: Ok action items logged. I'll open PRs: policy-schema, console-proto, telemetry-spec.

maria: Thanks all — let's sync next Tuesday for review. :thumbsup:

kevin: ack.

nate: Thanks!
